answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require every identity to lock a refundable stake that grows with each extra identity one operator controls, like felling timber: the first tree is cheap, the hundredth costs far more. A public atlas of reputation ties each stake to verifiable work history, so a fresh fake has nothing to borrow. If an agent cheats, its stake is slashed and the loss echoes across all its linked identities, so running a thousand sockpuppets costs a thousand stakes instead of one.
